notes.claim: Where two gears meet, their teeth move the same way, so the two gears rotate in opposite directions.
For two meshed gears, the speed of each multiplied by its tooth count is the same for both (N1 × Z1 = N2 × Z2).
An odd number of gears in a closed loop in a plane will not turn, whatever their sizes and tooth counts.

sources.title: Gears - Moments, levers and gears - AQA - GCSE Physics (Single Science) Revision - AQA - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Where the gears meet, the teeth must both move in the same direction. In the diagram, the teeth of both gears move upwards. This means that the gears rotate in opposite directions.

sources.title: Basic Fundamentals of Gear Drives
sources.quote: When gear 1 and gear 2 are in mesh: N1 * Z1 = N2 * Z2

sources.title: https://www.dsimanek.vialattea.net/gearprob.htm
sources.quote: An odd number of gears in a closed loop in a plane will not turn no matter what their size and tooth count.
